title: Urdais Power Delivery — PD-3 long-horizon planning demand
status: internal research; establishes no legal right; does not write code, design UI, or select a deliverable-capacity methodology

pd2_universe.note: PD-3 geography must align to PD-2 physical BA codes, not wholesale-price instruments

cleanest_planning_forecast_path.why: Only market that is both first-party hourly and rights-clean enough to publish with attribution. Latest complete published vintage is April 2025 ERCOT Adjusted Forecast; 2026 LTLF not finalized as of 2026-09-19.
Independent staff 20-year zonal/LDA/RTO forecast with Excel, hourly ZIPs, Previous Reports ZIP, and Manual 19 Attachment B large-load screen. Rights block public display.
CEC CED 2025 is the source of record, with CAISO-BAA hourly files and Known Loads split. CEC commercial-use sentence blocks public display pending legal review.

rights_blockers.issue: Website ToU forbids publish, distribute, or derivative works of website content
Commercial publication requires express written authorization
PRA public-use with credit plus a commercial/profit-making prohibition; scopes the CAISO planning-forecast gate
Not Data Miner, but website copyright still applies. Data Miner derived-data ban does not automatically attach.
Access confers no licence; IP reserved
Content copyrighted; non-personal duplication may violate copyright

methodology_blockers.issue: No public first-party vintageed MW demand time series at BA grain. Module E is participant-private. OMS-MISO is a 5-year resource survey CAGR. Dec 2024 whitepaper is CAGR trajectories, not a downloadable year-by-year Excel.
Public product is LRE-submitted Net Peak Demand in a 6-year RA report, not an independent ISO long-term load forecast. LRE workbooks not public.
Planning-area geography, no scenarios, no large-load documentation, mapping error-prone; cannot replace ISO forecasts for V1.

executive_conclusions.aggregation_rationale: Option B (sum of official peaks) mixes non-coincident peaks, time zones, peak seasons, weather bases, gross/net definitions, large-load screens, and vintages. Option C requires hourly planning profiles for all seven markets; only ERCOT, CEC CAISO, and PJM were confirmed to publish them. NYISO, MISO, and SPP lack public ISO-coincident 8760s; ISO-NE hourly methodology exists but the public workbook URL was not extracted.

ferc714_materially_improves_path.note: Annual vintage of 10-year summer/winter peak and annual energy. Useful for utility-level backfill. Not ISO coincident peak, not PD-2 BA geography, likely weak ERCOT coverage.

markets.source: 2025 Long-Term Demand and Energy Forecast (LTDEF / LTLF); CDR uses Adjusted Forecast
markets.publisher: Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc.
markets.current_vintage: April 2025 ERCOT Adjusted Forecast (hourly XLSB 2025-04-15). December 2025 CDR uses this vintage. 2026 LTLF not finalized as of 2026-09-19.
markets.forecast_horizon: Hourly files cover the next ~10 years (2025 report: 2025-2034/2035)
markets.publication_cadence: Annual LTLF intended; CDR semiannual intended. May 2026 CDR skipped load/reserve tables during recalibration.
markets.geographic_coverage: ERCOT region / eight weather zones. Lubbock and additional RCEC load are explicit adders. Aligns to PD-2 ERCO.
markets.large_load_treatment: TSP RFI. Contracts = signed agreement + financial commitment. Officer Letters = TSP officer attestation without signed agreement. Adjusted Forecast: 180-day delay; data-center requested MW x 49.8%; officer-letter MW x 55.4%. Types: hydrogen, data centers, crypto, oil and gas, industrial. LFL modeled separately. 2026 Batch Zero Base/Studied/Excluded paused for audit; verification report due 2026-12-10.
markets.historical_vintages: Current Load Forecast page lists 2025 LTLF files only. CDR archives exist on the Resource Adequacy page. Do not invent a complete LTLF hourly archive.
markets.format: XLSB hourly, XLSX peaks/energy/scenarios, DOCX/PDF methodology
markets.notes: Appendix A 2025 report: summer peak 85759 MW (2025), 94650 (2026), 144522 (2031). Net Forecast = Base + EV + LFL + Adjusted Contracts + Adjusted Officer Letters - PV. Freeze public series on April 2025 Adjusted until a finalized 2026 LTLF exists.

markets.source: 2026 Load Forecast Report + Tables/Data XLS + Long-Term Load Forecast Supplement
markets.publisher: PJM Interconnection (Resource Adequacy Planning Department, independent staff forecast)
markets.current_vintage: Posted 2026-01-14. Supplement 2026-02-06. Mid-year update 2026-07-24 informational only. Data Center Accuracy Report 2026-05-29.
markets.forecast_horizon: 20-year peaks, net energy, load management, distributed solar, PEVs, battery storage
markets.geographic_coverage: PJM RTO / Control Area as of the report, with zone incorporation dates (OVEC 2018-12-01, EKPC 2013-06-01, DOM 2005-05-01, etc.). Aligns to PD-2 PJM; store zone-set with vintage.
markets.large_load_treatment: Manual 19 Attachment B. EDC/LSE submissions >= 50 MW. ESO / Construction Commitment / Other. Firm (ESO or CC plus meaningful financial commitment) may affect RPM-period years; Non-Firm derated and generally excluded from near-term RPM years. 2026 implementation: typically >= 36-month ramp, ~70% utilization unless supported.
markets.historical_vintages: Previous Reports ZIP on the Load Forecast Development Process page.
markets.do_not_ingest_via: PJM Data Miner 2 (unsuitable_without_permission for redistribution of data or derivatives)
markets.notes: Published peaks are non-coincident unrestricted unless noted otherwise. 2026 vintage is lower than 2025 through 2032: -2564 MW / -1.6% for 2026 (3rd IA). Summer unrestricted RTO peak 222106 MW in 2036 (10-year +65733 MW).

markets.source: December 2024 Long-Term Load Forecast whitepaper; 2026 LTLF workshop. Not Module E public data. Not OMS-MISO as a demand series.
markets.current_vintage: Dec 2024 whitepaper is the latest independently extracted first-party document. A May 2026 whitepaper is referenced by stakeholders; CDN fetch returned HTTP 500. Do not treat press figures as verified.
markets.publication_cadence: Irregular workshops; not an annual Excel product analogous to PJM/CELT/Gold Book
markets.geographic_coverage: MISO footprint / 10 LRZs. Generally aligns to PD-2 MISO; LRZ 9 includes Louisiana and eastern Texas.
markets.large_load_treatment: Data centers are an explicit modeled driver in the 2024 whitepaper (149-241 TWh by 2044). No public ESO/CC-style inclusion screen found. Module E coincident peaks are LSE-submitted in MECT and participant-private.
markets.historical_vintages: Futures Series 1 (2021), 1A (2023), Series 2 (2026) are transmission-planning scenarios, not RA demand vintages. Dec 2024 LTLF is one published load-forecast vintage.
markets.format: PDF whitepaper; some Futures hourly XLSX on the Futures page
markets.notes: 122 GW in 2024 to 152-186 GW in 2044 per Dec 2024 whitepaper. OMS-MISO 2026: 3.1%-5.1% five-year member-reported load CAGR; capacity-oriented, not a PD-3 demand series. Weakest of the seven for a defensible PD-3 ingest.

markets.source: 2026 Summer Season Resource Adequacy Report (East BAA)
markets.forecast_horizon: Upcoming summer plus summer 2027 through summer 2031 (six-year class, not 10-20)
markets.geographic_coverage: SPP East BAA only. Not WEIS. Aligns to PD-2 SWPP.
markets.large_load_treatment: LREs submit Workbook Net Peak Demand. Workbooks are not public. No public ISO-level ESO/CC-style screen.
markets.ai_data_center_note: Secondary coverage of SPP's FERC information report discusses immature data-center interconnection requests in utility forecasts. Not independently extracted from the RA PDF as a source-published screen.
markets.historical_vintages: Prior-year RA reports exist as separate PDFs (e.g. 2024). This pass did not build a complete year list.
markets.format: PDF. Table 1 numeric cells not extracted as text. LRE workbooks not public.
markets.notes: 2026 summer: 65 LREs met RAR; ACAP PRM 7.06%; East BAA ACAP reserve margin 17.1% (~5752 MW excess above RAR). Existing-only resources: aggregate RAR deficiency beginning 2029; 28% increase in LRE Net Peak Demand by 2031. Do not invent 2026 Net Peak Demand MW. ITP is a different product.

markets.source: CEC California Energy Demand (CED) 2025 / 2025 IEPR. CAISO 2026 SLRA uses CED; it does not originate the planning forecast.
markets.publisher: California Energy Commission (forecast); CAISO (seasonal assessment citing CEC)
markets.current_vintage: CED 2025 adopted 2026-01-21 for years 2025-2045; some files extrapolated to 2050. SLRA 2026 uses CED 2025 1-in-2 Planning.
markets.geographic_coverage: CED CAISO hourly files align to PD-2 CISO. CED Total State / LADWP / SMUD / IID / BANC do not. Never substitute California statewide demand for CAISO BAA.
markets.large_load_treatment: Known Loads = utility energization requests; included in Local Reliability, excluded from 2025 Planning. Data centers = project-based utility applications; 67% utilization; confidence by signed agreement / active application / inquiry. SLRA: 2026 CAISO 1-in-2 Planning peak 46844 MW on 2026-09-02 HE18 PDT excluding Known Loads; Known Loads could add ~1569 MW.
markets.historical_vintages: CED 2024 Planning Forecast Updated LSE/BA tables posted on the CED 2025 page. Older IEPR/CEDU cycles exist as separate pages.
markets.notes: 1-in-5/10/20 peaks 49534 / 50872 / 52122 MW. SLRA load numbers are CEC CED numbers; CAISO website PRA language does not escape the CEC commercial-use clause.

markets.current_vintage: Posted 2026-04-29: Gold Book PDF; Baseline / Higher Demand / Lower Demand XLSX. Direct 2026 PDF URL attempted in this pass returned 404; 2026 cell-level MW not independently extracted.
markets.forecast_horizon: Energy and seasonal peaks through ~2055 in the 2025 Gold Book structure; treat 2026 similarly until 2026 PDF is extracted
markets.geographic_coverage: New York Control Area. Aligns to PD-2 NYIS.
markets.large_load_treatment: Table I-14 is not the interconnection queue. 2025 notes: tables do not necessarily reflect Table IV-7 queue MW/dates and include some non-queue projects. Higher/Lower scenarios scale large-load growth. Secondary coverage of 2026 Gold Book reports 538 MW 2026 summer large-load impact vs queue >12 GW (not verified from 2026 PDF).
markets.historical_vintages: Gold Book page lists 2026 and 2025. Library keeps current plus two previous years; See More for a longer listing.
markets.notes: 2025 Gold Book: most TOs 50th percentile peak weather; Con Edison and O&R 67th. Hydrogen electrolysis excluded from baseline. Wholesale storage is not a peak reducer. Confirm 2026 tables on ingest.

markets.current_vintage: CELT 2026 published 2026-05-01 covering 2026-2035 (ISO Newswire). CELT and Load Forecast page document tables were JS-empty; no direct XLSX URL extracted.
markets.forecast_horizon: 10-year CELT; some component discussion into the 2040s
markets.geographic_coverage: New England Control Area. Aligns to PD-2 ISNE.
markets.large_load_treatment: Debut in CELT 2026. Inclusion: >20 MW expected nameplate AND a formal study agreement. Near-term summer/winter limited to projects under construction. Final-draft: two projects (NEMA data center 200 MW; CT general electrification 85 MW); none under construction, so contribution to winter 2026/27 and summer 2026 and 2027 = 0.
markets.historical_vintages: Annual CELT series is the intended backfill path. Confirm file listing on ingest; do not invent years.
markets.machine_readable_caveat: Workbook URL not independently extracted in this pass
markets.notes: Material regional difference vs ERCOT/PJM: official near-term large-load contribution is zero because of the construction screen. ISO Newswire: ~110 MW peak in the 2030s, ~130 MW in the 2040s.

ferc714_fallback.form: FERC Form No. 714 Annual Electric Balancing Authority Area and Planning Area Report
ferc714_fallback.schedule: Part III Schedule 2 forecast block (summer peak MW, winter peak MW, annual net energy for load MWh, next ten years)
ferc714_fallback.filing_cadence: On or before June 1 for the preceding calendar year
ferc714_fallback.respondent_geography: Planning areas with peak load greater than 200 MW based on net energy for load; typical respondent is the principal resource-planning entity with obligation to serve. Balancing-authority filers are a separate 141.51(a)(1) class. Not 1:1 with PD-2 BAs.
ferc714_fallback.mapping_to_seven_markets: Possible only with a respondent crosswalk. PUDL notes utility-vs-BA ambiguity and CSV-vs-XBRL identifier differences. This pass did not produce a crosswalk and did not confirm an ERCOT Inc. filing. ERCOT FERC-jurisdictional status makes a 1:1 BA filing unlikely.
ferc714_fallback.data_quality: Filer-dependent completeness; footprints change with mergers; no scenario or large-load metadata; hourly actuals are standard-time
ferc714_fallback.useful_as: Rights-cleaner internal vintage backfill and diagnostic when ISO numbers diverge from in-footprint 714 respondents
ferc714_fallback.rights_note: U.S. government-works practice; no EIA-style FERC reuse page found. Classification is inferred, not a FERC grant.
